rationale: Stagehand is a TypeScript monorepo (v3.7.1, @browserbasehq/stagehand) providing AI-powered browser automation with four core methods: act(), extract(), observe(), and agent(). Its primary relevance to a scraping pipeline is the browser-automation concern: it handles all browser interaction (navigation, clicking, form filling, data extraction) via LLM-driven or CDP-based control. The framework includes self-healing selectors (actHandler.ts takeDeterministicAction, lines 332-420 retries actInference on failure), caching (ActCache.ts, AgentCache.ts persist action sequences keyed by SHA256 of instruction+URL), domain policy filtering (domainPolicy.ts), deep locator resolution across iframes and shadow DOM (deepLocator.ts), and a CAPTCHA solver integration via Browserbase (captchaSolver.ts). It supports 15+ LLM providers via the AI SDK. No evidence supports JSON-LD/Schema.org extraction, full-text search indexing, queue/job scheduling, fuzzy matching/dedupe, or standalone stealth features (Browserbase managed fingerprinting only). The repo is large (916 TS source files, 179 directories) with an eval suite (WebVoyager, OnlineMind2Web, WebTailBench, GAIA) and extensive unit/integration tests (~100 test files). Tier A: highest relevance for pipeline-scoped work on browser automation — a strong engine candidate for the extraction concern of a scraping pipeline, but not a complete pipeline on its own for the eight concerns listed.
limitations: No fuzzy matching or deduplication logic
No self-contained stealth/anti-bot features (relies on Browserbase managed fingerprinting, which is a cloud provider feature, not in-source)
No LLM script generation pipeline (act/agent execute actions, they do not generate standalone scripts)
Not a declared core candidate for the Veridian pipeline
Extract() uses LLM inference for structured data extraction, not programmatic parsing of structured markup
